currency_screening_decisions.rationale: University-student BMI and general fitness study; not a running-plan population or routing study.
Inspiratory-pressure reference interval study; not running-plan evidence.
Clinical geriatric depression treatment trial; excluded clinical treatment population and wrong intervention.
Post-knee-surgery runner cohort; excluded clinical and surgical recovery context.
Sleep-disorder treatment review; excluded clinical outcome and no running-plan routing evidence.
Caffeine and resistance-exercise meta-analysis in women; wrong exposure and no running-plan policy evidence.
Older-adult walking-function index; not a runner or plan-generation study.
Caffeine meta-analysis in female team-sport athletes; wrong sport and exposure.
Pediatric low-vision training trial; excluded child and clinical population.
Rat multi-omic endurance-training study; mechanistic animal evidence cannot define an adult running-plan route.
Cognitive-motor training review; wrong intervention and outcome.
Creatine supplementation review in older adults; supplement question, not running-plan routing.
Resistance-exercise BDNF study in older adults; wrong outcome and no running-plan route.
Military fitness-testing analysis; not recreational running-plan generation.

gap_query_screening_summaries.rationale: The query recovered the included women-masters scoping review plus health, aging, bone, vascular, and general-exercise sources. No result compared a menopause-specific running-plan family or dose rule.

The two included full-text studies describe transgender-women or nonbinary running performance and expose important limitations; the remaining records concern sport eligibility, general fitness, or non-running topics. No result compared running-plan prescriptions or established a gender-identity dose modifier.

screening_decisions.rationale: Systematic review and meta-analysis directly comparing injury incidence in novice and recreational runners.
Systematic review directly evaluating running injuries against distance, duration, frequency, intensity, and recent training changes.
Randomized novice-runner trial directly testing a 10 percent progression program against a standard program.
Randomized recreational-runner trial comparing intensity-focused and volume-focused progression schedules.
Prospective beginner-program study retained for completion, dropout, injury, and flexible-design limitations.
Systematic review and meta-analysis quantifying heterogeneous short- and long-term detraining effects in trained populations.
Systematic review describing endurance detraining while explicitly identifying insufficient evidence for an exact reduced-training dose.
Review of age-associated endurance performance and physiology in masters athletes, including preserved capabilities and training effects.
Review relating masters VO2max decline to training-volume change and training cessation rather than age alone.
Recovery review retained for its warning that activity level and nonrepresentative exercise protocols confound age comparisons.
Direct downhill-running study comparing recovery in younger and older endurance-trained adults.
Direct masters-runner interval study showing substantial inter-individual recovery variation at 24 hours.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of strength methods in middle- and long-distance runners with explicit certainty and population limits.
Randomized first-marathon study showing one self-directed strength program did not reduce overuse injury or improve finishing time.
Systematic review and meta-analysis showing limited, heterogeneous evidence for running-cycling transfer and no validated interchangeability rule.
Systematic review and meta-analysis separating similar overall injury rates from diagnosis-specific sex differences.
Systematic review and meta-analysis finding trivial average menstrual-cycle effects, high variability, and no basis for general phase rules.
Review retained for the documented underrepresentation and unresolved recovery and training questions in female masters athletes.
Scoping review of women masters endurance athletes documenting observational evidence, training-volume associations, and unresolved menopause effects.
Small heterogeneous transgender-women athlete study retained to bound observed performance and training-volume associations without converting them into a plan-family or dose rule.
Secondary nonbinary race-performance analysis retained to distinguish descriptive association from causal training response or prescription.
